blocks.text: I can form the letters u, y and j.
Your hands and wrists get stronger when you exercise them, just like any other muscle in your body.
Stronger hands and wrists help you to hold your pencil using your tripod grip.

items.title: Hand squeeze
items.sub: Squeeze your hand tight, then open it.

items.title: Wiper wrists
items.sub: Put your hands up like window wipers and wipe from one side to the other.

blocks.text: Practising writing patterns helps us to prepare for writing letters.
Today’s pattern goes **down and up, down and up, down and up**. Try it in the air with your finger and then with your fist.
Copy and continue the pattern using your tripod grip. Do not lift your pencil while you make the pattern.

items: The letter u is an x-height letter.
The letter u is a small letter.
It does not have an ascender.
The letter u finishes with a flick.

items.def: Letters that reach the middle height on the line.
The part of a letter that extends above the level of the top of an x.

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline.
3. Go across, and back up to the x-height line.
4. Go down, and finish with a flick.

blocks.text: Do not lift your pencil when you form the letter u.

blocks.q: Which is true about the letter u?
options: It is an x-height letter and finishes with a flick
blocks.why: The letter u is an x-height letter and finishes with a flick. It is a small letter with no ascender.

blocks.q: Which line does the letter u start on?
blocks.why: The letter u starts on the x-height line.

blocks.text: The letter y is formed in a similar way to the letter u. However, part of the letter y goes below the baseline.
The letter y falls below the baseline and curls up at the descender line. That is the line right at the bottom.

items.def: The part of a letter that descends below the level of the bottom of an x. It goes below the baseline.
The line that most letters sit on.

blocks.text: The letter y is an example of a letter with a descender.

items: 1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the baseline, go across, and back up to the x-height line.
3. Go all the way down to the descender line.
4. Finish with a curl up.

blocks.text: Do not lift your pencil when you form the letter y.

blocks.q: Which line does the letter y curl up at?
blocks.why: The letter y goes below the baseline and curls up at the descender line.

blocks.q: What do we call the part of a letter that goes below the baseline?
blocks.why: A descender is the part of a letter that goes below the baseline.

items: The letter j starts on the x-height line.
The letter j has a descender.
It has a curl up at the descender line.
It has a dot at the top.
1. Start on the x-height line.
2. Go down to the descender line and curl up.
3. Take your pencil off the page.
4. Put it back on to add a dot at the top.

blocks.q: Which is true about the letter j?
options: It has a dot at the top and a descender
blocks.why: The letter j starts on the x-height line, has a descender and has a dot at the top.

blocks.q: What do you do after the curl up on the letter j?
options: Take your pencil off and add a dot at the top
Add a cross on the x-height line
blocks.why: After the curl up, take your pencil off the page and add a dot at the top.

blocks.q: How does the main line of each letter finish (before any dot)? Tap a letter, then tap its column.

blocks.label: What is the same?
blocks.text: Letters u, y and j all start on the x-height line.

blocks.q: Match each keyword to its meaning.

pairs.b: The line that most letters sit on
The part of a letter that goes below the baseline
A letter that reaches the middle height on the line
Holding the pencil with three fingers: thumb, index and middle

items: The letter u is an x-height letter. It goes down, around, back up, down and finishes with a flick.
The letter y is like a u but goes below the baseline to the descender line and curls up.
The letter j goes down, curls up and has a dot at the top.
The letters j and y have descenders.
The letters u, y and j all start on the x-height line.

flashcards.back: An x-height letter. It is a small letter with no ascender.

flashcards.back: It is formed in a similar way, but part of the y goes below the baseline.

flashcards.front: Where does the letter y curl up?

flashcards.back:
The part of a letter that goes below the baseline.

The letters y and j have descenders.

flashcards.front: How is the letter j formed?
flashcards.back: Go down to the descender line, curl up, then take the pencil off and add a dot at the top.

flashcards.front: What do you add to the top of the letter j?
Which of u, y and j have descenders?

flashcards.front: Why do we warm up our hands before writing?
flashcards.back: Our hands and wrists get stronger when we exercise them. Strong hands help us hold the pencil in the tripod grip.
